newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade dull.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade dull.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were generally stable in late trading on Thursday but buying interest remained thin, traders said.
They said olein was generally quoted at 1,435-40 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, but offers were also heard at 1,430 rupiah.
Crude palm oil was done at an equivalent of 1,222 rupiah/kg at a 500-tonne tender in the North Sumatran city of Medan, virtually unchanged from the previous tender price.
"Crude palm oil is staying stable due to good export prices," one trader said. "Olein, on the other hand, is showing signs it might weaken."
Meanwhile, a port official said delays in loading the MV Antea at Belawan Port in North Sumatra had been overcome and that the vessel set sail for Malaysia early on Wednesday.
He said the 16,689-tonne vessel was carrying 3,000 tonnes of crude palm oil to Malaysia's Port Klang, where it was expected to berth on Friday morning.
The loading delays, due to contamination of its tanks by a previous vegetable oil cargo, had caused a brief squeeze and lifted crude palm oil offer prices in Europe.
Data from Belawan Port showed that the MV Pershing will leave on Saturday for Tanjung Priok with 4,600 tonnes of olein.
